newsitem.title: USA: Sears Q2 net expected higher before items.
newsitem.headline: Sears Q2 net expected higher before items.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co was expected to report Thursday that its earnings increased in the second quarter before extraordinary items.
The retailer was expected to post earnings of $0.74 a share for the period compared to $0.67 a share in the same period last year, according to First Call.
The estimate excludes several extraordinary items.

During the second quarter, the company said it would record a charge to cover the costs of a settlement with state attorneys general and class-action plaintiffs from its improper handling of debt reaffirmation agreements.

Sears agreed to pay between $178 million and $265 million a share to settle the claims. Some Wall Street analysts at the time estimated the company would record a charge of $0.31 to $0.44 a share, although a more recent estimate by one analyst put the charge at between $0.50 and $0.75 a share.

In addition, Sears sold its 30-percent stake in data network services provider Advantis to International Business Machines Corp, which owned the other 70 percent of Advantis. In June, Sears said it would record an after-tax gain from the sale of about $90 million, or $0.23 a share.
